title: TF 2.13.0-rc0 fails to compile on Ubuntu 22.04
body: I am compiling TensorFlow 2.13.0-rc0 from source on Ubuntu 22.04 x86_64 with Python 3.10.6, Bazel 5.3.0, and GCC 11.3.0. With the default ./configure choices, the pip-package build fails. The same failure occurs with or without CUDA 11.8 support.

symptoms_visible: The TensorFlow 2.13.0-rc0 pip-package build stops before completing on Ubuntu 22.04 when I use the default configure parameters.
I see the build failure both with CUDA 11.8 enabled and with CUDA disabled.
N0.label: N0 Ubuntu source-build failure reported

symptoms_visible: On my x86_64 Ubuntu system, the build reports that @local_config_python//:<nick> is a genrule without outputs and aborts analysis of //tensorflow/tools/pip_package:build_pip_package.
N1.label: N1 architecture and first actionable error known

symptoms_visible: TensorFlow 2.12.0 now fails on this Ubuntu machine as well, with or without CUDA, even though I was able to compile that release when it originally came out.
N2.label: N2 failure shown not to be specific to 2.13 release candidate

symptoms_visible: The Ubuntu build fails when my installed Cython is newer than 0.29.28, including with 0.29.32.
Using Cython 0.29.28 lets the build complete; that is also the version available from Ubuntu through apt.
N3.label: N3 Cython version dependency isolated

symptoms_visible: TensorFlow 2.13.0 compiles successfully when I use the compatible library versions.
The outcome depends on the Cython version rather than on whether the source is an earlier release candidate or the final 2.13.0 release.
N4.label: N4 successful build confirmed with compatible dependency

symptoms_visible: The TensorFlow source build completes on Ubuntu after I use Cython 0.29.28 instead of a newer Cython release.
N_terminal.label: terminal Ubuntu build resolved

question_patterns: What system architecture are you building on?
Is the Ubuntu machine x86_64, ARM64, or another architecture?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It is an ARM64 Ubuntu system rather than x86_64.
It is x86_64, and the machine has a Quadro RTX 6000.

edges.comment: From c5 on the original reporter's Ubuntu system: after being asked for the architecture, the reporter answered x86_64 and also pasted the actionable local_config_python genrule error. The pasted error is represented as target-node volunteered information.

question_patterns: Can you build TensorFlow 2.12.0 with the same Ubuntu configuration and report whether its behavior differs?
Please test the previous TensorFlow release on this machine to determine whether this began with 2.13.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On Ubuntu 22.04, TensorFlow 2.12.0 fails just as well with Python 3.10.6, GCC 11.3.0, Bazel 5.3.0, and either CUDA 11.8 or no CUDA. It compiled fine when 2.12.0 was originally released, so I am not sure what changed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: TensorFlow 2.12.0 builds successfully in the same environment, while 2.13.0-rc0 consistently fails.
TensorFlow 2.12.0 produces the same failure only when CUDA is enabled.

edges.comment: From c6 and c8, describing only the original reporter's Ubuntu setup: a maintainer requested a 2.12.0 comparison, and the reporter found the same failure despite remembering that 2.12.0 had built successfully when released.

question_patterns: Can you compare the installed Python build packages with a clean environment where the build succeeds and report which version difference reproduces the failure?
Could you isolate whether changing any installed Python package version changes the Ubuntu build result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I finally isolated it: compilation fails when Cython newer than 0.29.28 is installed. The latest version I tested was 0.29.32, and that failed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Changing Cython versions makes no difference; both 0.29.28 and 0.29.32 produce the same error.

question_patterns: Can you rerun the build using the setup from the successful comparison and report whether it completes?
Please repeat the build with the package versions from the working setup and tell us the observed result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With Cython 0.29.28, the Ubuntu compilation succeeds. That is also the Cython version Ubuntu provides through apt.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The build still fails with Cython 0.29.28, so that version does not resolve it.

edges.comment: From c12 and c14 on the original reporter's Ubuntu system. The reporter independently compared package versions and produced the observed pass/fail boundary. This is modeled as a diagnostic measurement; the separate macOS realpath problem from c7 and c13 is deliberately excluded from the Ubuntu chain.

question_patterns: Could you try the final TensorFlow 2.13.0 source release in the environment you have been testing and report whether it compiles?
Please rerun the build with TensorFlow 2.13.0 and tell us the observed result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, TensorFlow 2.13.0 compiles fine. It is not because the final release differs from the earlier release candidates for this issue; it works because I am using the correct library versions.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: TensorFlow 2.13.0 still fails with the same local_config_python genrule error in the environment where the earlier build worked.
TensorFlow 2.13.0 compiles successfully, but the build takes longer than the release candidate did.

edges.comment: From c19-c20 on the original reporter's system: a maintainer requested a current-release retest, and the reporter confirmed a successful 2.13.0 build while explicitly attributing the changed outcome to compatible libraries rather than the release transition.

solution.intent: Use Cython 0.29.28 for this Ubuntu source build, avoid an unsupported newer Cython release, and document the required Cython version among the source-build prerequisites.
solution.concrete_example: Install or pin Cython 0.29.28, such as the version supplied by Ubuntu apt, then clean and rebuild TensorFlow. The source-build requirements should state this compatible Cython version rather than allowing the latest 0.29.x package implicitly.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter directly supplied the Cython pass/fail comparison. Combining that comparison with the same failure on TensorFlow 2.12.0, success after using compatible libraries, and independence from CUDA supports the broader conclusion that this is an environment dependency-compatibility problem rather than a TensorFlow 2.13 release-candidate regression.

edges.comment: Resolution from c12, c14, c20, and c22 on the original reporter's Ubuntu system: Cython 0.29.28 builds successfully, newer Cython versions fail, and the requested project action is documentation of the version requirement rather than a TensorFlow source change. Later participant5 reports concern a different Docker/Clang/CUDA deployment and are not merged into this causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted Ubuntu root cause: the source build fails with Cython versions newer than 0.29.28, while Cython 0.29.28 permits the build to complete.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: the local_config_python genrule error, the same failure on TensorFlow 2.12.0, the Cython version comparison, and the successful TensorFlow 2.13.0 rebuild with compatible libraries.
Must recommend using or pinning Cython 0.29.28 and documenting that compatible version in the TensorFlow source-build requirements.
Must not misdiagnose the Ubuntu issue as CUDA-specific or as a regression unique to TensorFlow 2.13.0-rc0; it occurred without CUDA and also affected 2.12.0 in the changed environment.
Must not conflate the Ubuntu Cython issue with the separate macOS realpath problem or the later participant's Docker/Clang/CUDA build problem.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter confirms that the source build completes with the compatible dependency version.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced source-build user who can configure Bazel, compare TensorFlow releases and CUDA configurations, inspect detailed build errors, and isolate Python dependency versions.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, technically detailed, and persistent; supplies exact versions and error excerpts, rejects unrelated reproduction failures, and emphasizes missing build documentation after finding the workaround.
